Hi Eve —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is an initial draft matrix (RDW_SIG_Hosting_ResponsibilityMatrix_v0.xlsx) that maps the items you listed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. High-level notes here so you can skim before we attach the fuller evidence pack: 

- Hosted API: Redwood owns runtime patching, kernel/hypervisor updates, full stack encryption at rest. Key management: Redwood-managed keys by default; we offer customer-supplied KMS integration for enterprise accounts (BYOK). Audit logs: we provide tenant-level logs via the Console API (retention configurable for Dedicated).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Patching and host-level maintenance are coordinated — Redwood handles software runtime updates; customer controls network boundary. For dedicated clusters we can provide longer log retention and exportable logs on request.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer is responsible for physical network and host OS; Redwood provides the control plane and deployment artifacts. For on-prem we support a customer-managed KMS pattern (BYOK) and can offer an air-gapped package for regulated workloads.

I also put a short evidence index on the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExample (RDW_SIG_EvidenceIndex.pdf will be added in the final package). Can you confirm whether the matrix + indexed PDFs are sufficient, or do you need separate signed extracts (SOC 2 pages, architecture diagrams in Visio, etc.)?

If that format works we’ll refine the matrix and circulate a final package by mid next week.

Cheers,
Ava Chen

Summary (high level) — please see the attached matrix for row-level detail:

Hosted API (Redwood-managed runtime)
- Patching & runtime updates: Redwood
- Key custody: Redwood-managed keys by default; enterprise BYOK via KMS integration (customer key material stored in their KMS, envelope encryption used by Redwood runtime)
- Network: Public endpoints by default; private endpoints (VPC peering, private link) available for enterprise tiers
- Audit logs: Tenant-level logs exposed via Console API; standard retention 30 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated
- Incident response: Redwood first responder; customer notified per escalation policy in attached SLA excerpt

Dedicated / Reserved Capacity
- Patching: Redwood coordinates and applies application/runtime updates; host-level maintenance windows are scheduled with the customer
- Key custody: BYOK strongly recommended; Redwood can configure customer KMS or use Redwood-managed keys per contract
- Network: Customer-controlled perimeter (VPCs) with optional private peering; public egress limited by default
- Audit logs: Exportable logs; longer retention available via export to customer S3 or longer retention config
- Incident response: Shared model — Redwood handles runtime incidents; customer handles host/infra where they operate it (documented in SOW)

Private / VPC / On-prem
- Patching: Customer responsible for host OS and physical server maintenance; Redwood provides deployment artifacts and control-plane guidance where applicable
- Key custody: Customer manages KMS in all private/on-prem deployments (BYOK); Redwood provides integration guidance only
- Network: Customer fully controls network topology; Redwood recommends private endpoints and avoids public ingress in on-prem packages
- Audit logs: Local log retention and SIEM integration are customer responsibilities; we provide log format and ingestion guidance
- Incident response: Customer leads initial incident handling for host/network; Redwood provides application-level support per contract

Evidence included in the RDW_SIG_EvidenceIndex.pdf (attached): SOC 2 Type II (redacted), architecture diagrams for each hosting option, KMS/BYOK integration guide, log retention/format spec, SLA excerpt for Dedicated customers. If you need signed extracts of specific SOC 2 sections, we can provide redacted extracts or direct you to our compliance portal.

Next steps: let us know if the matrix + evidence index meet your procurement checklist. If you prefer a short walkthrough, I’m available for a 30-min call next week.

Thanks —
